work.title: Piano Sonata No. 23 in F minor, ‘Appassionata’
work.movement: III. Allegro ma non troppo — Presto

version.note: The original solo-piano finale is identified, but the performing edition and editorial alterations are not documented. Commentary uses the original edition, plate 521. Its repeat of development plus recapitulation is supported by recurring contours in this recording’s analysis; this does not identify Schnabel’s score or establish an edit/take-splice history. The source’s attacca from movement II is distinct from separate-file playback spacing.

performers.note: The selected file’s artist tag, Archive description and Bloesch agree. The session list records a Bechstein piano, without an established serial number.

date.note: The Archive’s specific Op. 57 description gives 11.IV.1933, corroborated by the discography and reissue documentation. The general compilation date 1932 is not used for this sonata. The embedded date tag 2001 and repository upload in 2020 do not establish a session or transfer date.

place.value: Abbey Road Studios, Studio No. 3, London, England
place.note: Bloesch’s work entry identifies Abbey Road Studios, London, and the chronological session list specifies Studio No. 3 and a Bechstein piano.

label.note: His Master’s Voice issued the original recording. The actual pressing or subsequent reissue used to produce the selected MP3 is not identified, so its source-carrier label remains unknown.

catalogue.note: The historical complete-sonata issue was HMV DB 2215–2217 in Beethoven Sonata Society Volume 5, part of set DB 2211–2217. That original catalogue is documented, but no source-carrier or reissue catalogue is established for this digital file.

matrixTakeSides.note: Bloesch assigns the finale to historical sides 2B 6609 and 2B 6610, takes 1; the release-set catalogue lists 2B 6609I and 2B 6610I. Those original issued-side identifiers do not independently establish the take identities, source pressing or side-join location in this MP3.

credits.note: No transfer or restoration engineer is identified for the selected file. Archive uploader recordplayer78 is not assumed to be its engineer or owner. The independently consulted Pristine transfer credits Andrew Rose, but no upstream relationship with this MP3 is documented; that credit is not imported.

date.note: The item was added/public on 27 March 2020. Its MP3 carries date tag 2001 without identifying the event or release represented. Neither date is accepted as the analogue-transfer date.

processing.value: The embedded encoder tag states ‘Audiograbber 1.83.01, LAME dll 3.99, 256 Kbit/s, Joint Stereo, Normal quality’.
processing.note: The inspected selected stream contains MP3 audio at 44,100 Hz, two channels and 256,000 bit/s, with an attached JPEG image. Joint-stereo encoding is not evidence of an original stereo session. Analogue equipment, equalisation, restoration, noise reduction, speed/pitch correction and edit history remain unknown. Archive’s inventory calls the file ‘VBR MP3’; that repository label is distinguished from the stream and embedded encoder information.

digital.format: MP3; inspected audio 256 kb/s, 44.1 kHz, two channels; Archive format label VBR MP3

composition.value: The underlying Beethoven composition is public domain under the ordinary EU life-plus-70 term.
composition.note: Beethoven died in 1827. The viewable original score supplies historical musical evidence, not clearance of an unidentified modern performing edition. The composition’s term is separate from the recording’s rights.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: original sound recording first published in 1934.
recording.note: The Public Domain Project release-set catalogue explicitly states first release in 1934 for HMV DB 2211–2217. Bloesch identifies Op. 57 as DB 2215–2217, matrices 2B 6605–6610, distinguishing publication evidence from the 11 April 1933 session. Under the programme’s territorial EU rule, the earlier 50-year term expired before the 2013 extension. US status is not established and no worldwide clearance is claimed. The Archive Public Domain Mark is not an ownership release; the Public Domain Project’s worldwide/US expiry table is not adopted. No CC licence or independently established additional rights in an unidentified modern transfer are asserted.

rights.creditLine: Ludwig van Beethoven, Piano Sonata No. 23, Op. 57, III. Allegro ma non troppo — Presto; Artur Schnabel, piano. Recorded 11 April 1933, Abbey Road Studio No. 3, London; original HMV issue in Beethoven Sonata Society Volume 5. Selected MP3 from Internet Archive item beethovenschnabel6; transferred carrier and engineer unknown. Territorial EU recording basis; US status not established.

sources.title: David Bloesch — Artur Schnabel: A Discography (1987), Schnabel Music Foundation reproduction
sources.locator: Printed p. 47, entry 49: Op. 57, matrices 2B 6605/10, Abbey Road Studios, 11 April 1933, original HMV DB 2215/7 in Volume 5. Printed p. 89: Studio No. 3, Bechstein; finale sides 2B 6609 and 6610, takes 1. The introduction credits access to EMI recording logs; relevant scan pages inspected visually.

sources.title: Pristine Classical PAKM043 — Schnabel Beethoven Piano Sonatas, volume 7
sources.locator: Op. 57 session 11 April 1933, Abbey Road Studio 3, HMV DB 2215–17, matrices 2B 6605–10. This separate reissue corroborates the historical recording only; its durations and engineer are not assigned to the selected MP3.

sources.title: Public Domain Project Mediapool — HMV DB 2211–2217 release set
sources.locator: Release set information explicitly gives first release date 1934, HMV, DB 2211–2217, Op. 57, and matrices 2B 6605II through 2B 6610I. The 12 April 1933 recording reference is for the coupled Op. 22, not Op. 57. The page’s worldwide/US copyright-expiry table is not relied upon.

sources.title: Beethoven-Haus — Op. 57 original edition, Bureau des Arts et d’Industrie, plate 521
sources.locator: Sammlung Jean Van der Spek, J. Van der Spek C op. 57. Complete finale printed pp. 17–25 inspected, with the Andante join on p. 16. Start-repeat at the development and alternative endings after recapitulation; p. 24 includes sempre più allegro and Presto. Timing estimates combine this score order with the analysed recording; no reviewed bar-level alignment is claimed.

sources.title: Beethoven-Haus — Sonata for piano in F minor, Op. 57
sources.locator: Composition chronology 1804–first half 1806, dedication and original-edition identification. The nickname’s later history is kept separate from the composition’s original title.

sources.title: IMSLP — Piano Sonata No. 23, Op. 57, catalogue information
sources.locator: General Information: first publication 1807, Vienna, Bureau des Arts et d’Industrie; work dates and solo-piano movements. The Beethoven-Haus first-edition scan, not a blocked IMSLP PDF download, supplies the inspected notation.

sources.title: Schnabel Music Foundation — Artur Schnabel
sources.locator: Complete Berlin Beethoven sonata cycles in 1927 and January–April 1933. No claim that these were the first complete cycles by any pianist is adopted.

sources.title: Radio Record — Sunday programmes, issue of 28 December 1934
sources.locator: Volume VIII, issue 25, p. 22, Sunday 30 December: alternative programme 1YX, 8 p.m., ‘An Hour with Beethoven’, featuring Schnabel playing the Appassionata. This is contemporary public-presence evidence, not a matrix/catalogue identification or first-release day. The unrelated BBC recorded programme elsewhere in the listing is not attributed to this sonata.
